evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Argues from the hover-preview case that storing state in a widget's text breaks, and establishes one-way data flow: model -> render() -> widget, never the reverse.

If state lives in button['text'], a hover preview and a real move become indistinguishable. -- confirmed -- notebook 17-18's FakeButton model demonstrates it, and Debug Lab 3 makes it concrete: with a widget-reading win check, hovering three empty cells of one line declares a win with no clicks.

It is fine for a button to temporarily show something other than the model, provided the model stays the source of truth. -- confirmed against the real app -- during a hover buttons[4]['text'] == 'X' while state.board[4] == '', and the next render() restores the widget from the model.

Data flows model -> render() -> view and never the other way. -- confirmed with one documented exception -- tic_tac_toe.py explicitly annotates on_cell_enter/on_cell_leave and pulse_winning_line as deliberate presentation-only writes that do not touch state, consistent with the lesson rather than a violation.
